newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares fade away at close on Prodi worries.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares fade away at close on Prodi worries.

text.p: Italian shares slid to a lower close on Tuesday following the decline in bonds and the lira reflecting concern over Prime Minister Romano Prodi's political problems while stocks ignored other higher bourses elsewhere.

The market got off to a shakey start after technical problems halted screen-based trading soon after the opening. But then stocks showed signs of taking support from the lira's weekend return to the ERM before worries over Prodi returned to undermine overseas investors confidence.
The all-share Mibtel ended off 0.65 percent at 10,424 while the Mib30 index closed 0.68 percent down at 15,574.

Prodi has denied a conflict of interest after a magistrate demanded that he be sent for trial over alleged irregularities when he was head of IRI, but leaders of the PDS Massimo D'Alema said if Prodi fell there would have to be new elections.
Dealers said that investors were concerned over the Prodi developments and were ignoring the firmer start to Wall Street and a better trend to many European bourse.

Among stocks, Olivetti ended off 1.77 percent at 554.4 lire after news its ex-chairman Carlo De Benedetti's French holding Cerus is to sell its 48.05 percent stake in Spain's Cofir via a private international placement with institutions.
Pirelli ended off 1.38 percent at 2,720 lire after it denied a Tokyo market rumour that it was planning a sale of its Pirelli-Armstrong U.S. tyre unit to Japan's Bridgestone.
Fiat shed 2.65 percent to 4,476 lire, but ENI continued to see good support ending up 0.09 percent at 7,925 lire.
Financial holding group Gemina closed up 3.17 percent at 794.7 lire with talk that shares were undervalued.
